svg.title: Context Graph — complete system architecture
svg.desc: Local Kubernetes architecture: authenticated JSON, image and video ingestion through Vert.x; schema-validated Kafka; Flink graph and temporal processing; Iceberg and Kafka outputs; DuckDB GraphQL queries, Reactor Flux subscriptions, and a separate dashboard. OIDC and a check-only SpiceDB proxy enforce entity permissions. Separate media, recovery state, configuration and operator controls are shown. Matching lettered ports are explicit logical connections.

g.text: From arbitrary JSON and streamed media to temporal metrics, connected entities, and authorized experiences.
Workspace-wide reads • restricted entities need grants • writes require writer/admin
APIs verify issuer, audience, subject, expiry
No policy writes with API credentials
Both Vert.x APIs connect through B
No positive permission cache; fail closed
Restrict, grant and revoke through operator only
API, auth, Kafka, Polaris and S3 use verified TLS; identities and network policies limit access.
Validate input and output JSON Schema
Input video topic also feeds subscriptions ↓
JSON Pointer projections and graph extraction
Polaris REST · 2 replicas · persistent catalog P
events / nodes / edges / metrics; labeled rows
Reader and writer identities are separate
Private backends; no direct user credentials
Checkpoint-aligned sinks; Kafka may lead committed Iceberg history.
v5.2 · 2 replicas · only registered, labeled table schemas
Unique consumer group per API replica
Topic / entity routing + permission per event
Authorize EACH source BEFORE joins / aggregates
Edges require access to BOTH endpoints
Separate service · browser UI + Nginx proxy
Bearer token + workspace on queries / WS init
No direct file access · no data volume mounted
Browser / HLS.js ⇄ Nginx ⇄ ingestion authorization ⇄ RustFS media
Every file, playlist and range request rechecks access; active transfers check revocation and expiry.
jobs.yaml → sources, transforms, windows, Kafka / Iceberg sinks
query.yaml + queries.yaml → schemas, SQL, GraphQL + routing
Incremental RocksDB checkpoints · 10s interval / 5s min pause
Retained checkpoints + upgrade / hourly savepoints + HA metadata
RustFS recovery bucket · native savepoints · Kafka buffers input
Kubernetes Secrets, service identities and enforced NetworkPolicies
Firewall-only kube-router · API → check proxy; direct SpiceDB / PG blocked
Rolling replicas + PDBs + readiness + request drain; schema/ACL provisioning
Candidate Flink jobs: isolate state, groups, transactions, topics and tables
Solid → data / media Dashed → control / authorization Matching A / B / C / E / M / P / R ports are explicit connections, repeated to keep routes readable.
Single-node RustFS and single PostgreSQL are not HA. Savepoint upgrades pause job output. Production needs HA storage/DB, HTTPS ingress and OIDC PKCE.
